set_text.text: Warehouse capacity is how much stock a building can hold once aisles, dock and office are taken out. It is best counted in cases, through pallet positions and stack height. Square feet on a lease is only where the count starts.
Square feet is the landlord's unit, pallet positions are the warehouse's, and cases are the buyer's. Capacity means the last one: 12,400 cases here.
The ceiling assumes every position is filled. Receiving needs open slots to put product away, so a working building runs below it.
Food ships oldest first, so a new delivery often cannot go in front of older stock. One item can then hold two positions at once.
Who uses a warehouse size calculator
It is for independent food distributors working out what their current building holds. Anyone buying a bulk deal, booking a big inbound load or pricing new racking should check it.
